title: Security Automation Pipeline
summary: Python security automation pipeline that detects suspicious authentication activity, enriches alerts with threat intelligence, calculates explainable risk and confidence scores, maps activity to MITRE ATT&CK, and generates analyst-ready incident reports with human approval before response actions.
screenshotAlt: HTML security incident report showing a critical finding, an 86 out of 90 risk score, and a 10 out of 10 confidence score

details.overview: Python security automation pipeline that detects suspicious authentication activity, enriches alerts with threat intelligence, calculates explainable risk and confidence scores, maps activity to MITRE ATT&CK, and generates analyst-ready incident reports with human approval before response actions.
details.focus: Security automation and detection engineering for suspicious sign-in activity, built as a portfolio project with synthetic scenarios.
covered: 14 suspicious sign-in detection rules, including brute force, password spray, impossible travel, MFA fatigue, and success-after-failure correlation
Explainable risk scoring kept separate from confidence scoring
MITRE ATT&CK mapping and analyst-ready incident reports
Human-in-the-loop response approval and dry-run / safe response design
Automated pytest coverage using synthetic security scenarios
details.results: The pipeline turns authentication activity into an explainable alert: detection findings, enrichment, separate risk and confidence scores, ATT&CK mapping, and an incident report. Response actions stay behind human approval.

title: Kubernetes RBAC Security Lab
summary: Hands-on Kubernetes security lab demonstrating authentication, least-privilege RBAC, workload identity, Pod Security Admission, Calico NetworkPolicy, audit logging, controlled RBAC misconfiguration and remediation, and automated authorization testing.
screenshotAlt: Automated Kubernetes RBAC authorization test matrix with 15 passed checks and 0 failed

details.overview: Hands-on Kubernetes security lab demonstrating authentication, least-privilege RBAC, workload identity, Pod Security Admission, Calico NetworkPolicy, audit logging, controlled RBAC misconfiguration and remediation, and automated authorization testing.
details.focus: A learning lab for cloud-native security controls. It is not a production cluster.
covered: X.509 certificate authentication, and the difference between authentication and authorization
Namespace-scoped Roles and RoleBindings, plus least-privilege ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings
ServiceAccount workload identity, RBAC misconfiguration, privilege-expansion testing, and remediation
Pod Security Admission, Calico NetworkPolicy, and Kubernetes audit logging
kubectl auth can-i, kubectl-who-can, and 15 automated authorization checks
Bash and YAML automation with reproducible setup, cleanup, and GitHub Actions checks
details.results: The lab shows which identities can and cannot act, then proves it with 15 authorization checks. A controlled misconfiguration is introduced and then remediated.
